guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Preserve the Repository Governance Layer boundary: WIII informs external agents but does not schedule, retry, cancel, or manage them.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: The design and plan retain repository-local, read-only query boundaries and explicitly prohibit scheduler, retry, cancellation, workflow-engine, and agent-manager behavior; independent design review found no boundary expansion.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Distinguish authoritative source evidence from derived runtime projections and from non-authoritative activity observations.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: The design separates source-bound governance projections from runtimeObservation and assigns implementation to source/version, keyed-reducer, and API-boundary successor Work Items.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Treat all performance values as measured evidence only when their profile, sample size, workload, and environment are recorded.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: The design labels all latency values as candidates and the plan requires Task 4 to record workload, profile, environment, and at least 30 samples before any enforcement gate.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Do not claim a successor Work Item, provider check, merge, or cleanup completed until its own evidence exists.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: The design states that no V2 behavior is implemented, and the plan requires independent Contract, PR, hosted-check, merge, and ai-close-work-item evidence for every successor.

risk.detail: Documentation-only governance design; successor implementation Work Items will carry behavior and performance risk.

observedIssues.detail: The first documentation metadata check rejected the new plan for missing front matter and both new documents for missing documentation context registry entries. The plan received required metadata, both documents were registered as current instructions, and the check then passed.

residualRisks.detail: The design cannot itself prove WIII V2 correctness, compatibility, scalability, or provider lifecycle behavior; each claim remains assigned to a separately verified successor Work Item.

reviewReadiness.reason: All required verification passed; residual risk remains documented.

knownGaps: No production WIII behavior is changed by this design Work Item.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A confirmed semantic or integrity finding is translated into a bounded successor Work Item
evidence: Independent design review verified each disposition has implementation and test evidence or an explicit gap.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A suggested performance value lacks a reproducible baseline
evidence: The design requires profile, workload, environment, and at least 30 samples before a candidate budget becomes enforceable.
Task 4 defines the characterization harness and Task 6 consumes its profile-bound evidence.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A later Work Item uses the recorded user authorization for PR closure
evidence: Global Constraints require each successor Contract to record raw request/source, restricted approval where needed, exact governed artifact scope, PR merge, and ai-close-work-item branch cleanup.
The plan excludes release, tags, provider configuration, archive rewrites, and unrelated cleanup.

overclaimPrevention: Do not report completion for checks or behavior that were not verified.

checks.reason: The design dispositions map to successor tasks, tests, dependencies, and complete lifecycle requirements.
The Contract acceptance, authorization record, scope, and Summary evidence describe the same documentation-only Work Item.
New governed documents are registered and retain the documented WIII local, non-scheduler boundary.
This Work Item adds English design and plan records only; it changes no translated user-facing command or capability text.
The design explicitly records unimplemented V2 behavior, candidate-only performance targets, and the required successor evidence.
